questions.sub: Making of the Constitution
questions.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, which was constituted on 29 August 1947.

questions.sub: Making of the Constitution
questions.question: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.sub: Preamble
questions.question: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, inserted 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' into the Preamble.

questions.sub: Fundamental Rights
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form; its enforcement is a punishable offence.

questions.sub: Fundamental Rights
questions.question: The Right to Constitutional Remedies, which allows a citizen to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights, is guaranteed under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 32 guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies; Dr. Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

questions.sub: Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution contains the Directive Principles of State Policy, which are non-justiciable.

questions.sub: Fundamental Duties
questions.question: Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution on the recommendation of which committee, through the 42nd Amendment?
questions.explanation: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended inclusion of Fundamental Duties, added as Part IVA (Article 51A) by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.

questions.sub: Union Executive: President, Vice-President, PM, Council of Ministers
questions.question: The minimum age required to be eligible for election as President of India is:
questions.explanation: Article 58 requires a candidate for President to have completed 35 years of age.

questions.sub: Union Executive: President, Vice-President, PM, Council of Ministers
questions.question: Who acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?

options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Under Article 64, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.sub: Parliament: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, legislative procedure
questions.question: A Money Bill, as defined under Article 110, can be introduced only in:

options.C: Either House with prior Presidential assent
options.D: A joint sitting of both Houses

questions.explanation: Article 110 read with Article 109 provides that a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, on the recommendation of the President.

questions.sub: Parliament: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, legislative procedure
questions.question: What is the maximum permissible gap between two sessions of Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 85 requires that not more than six months shall intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.

questions.sub: Judiciary: Supreme Court, High Courts, judicial review
questions.question: In which case did the Supreme Court of India propound the 'Basic Structure' doctrine?

options.B: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
options.C: Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
options.D: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)

questions.explanation: The 13-judge bench in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) held that Parliament cannot amend the 'basic structure' of the Constitution.

questions.sub: Judiciary: Supreme Court, High Courts, judicial review
questions.question: The Gauhati High Court, which has jurisdiction over Mizoram, has a permanent Bench located at:
questions.explanation: The Gauhati High Court has a permanent Bench at Aizawl for Mizoram, along with Benches at Kohima (Nagaland) and Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh); the erstwhile Imphal and Agartala benches became the separate Manipur and Tripura High Courts in 2013.

questions.sub: Federalism and Centre-State relations
questions.question: Under which List of the Seventh Schedule does 'Police' fall, making it primarily a state subject?
questions.explanation: 'Police' is Entry 2 of the State List (List II) of the Seventh Schedule, making law and order primarily a state responsibility.

questions.sub: Emergency provisions
questions.question: Under which Article can the President declare a National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion?
questions.explanation: Article 352 empowers the President to proclaim a National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion (the term 'internal disturbance' was replaced by 'armed rebellion' via the 44th Amendment).

questions.sub: Emergency provisions
questions.question: A Proclamation of Financial Emergency is issued under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 360 empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency if the financial stability or credit of India is threatened; it has never been invoked so far.

questions.sub: Constitutional amendments
questions.question: Which amendment to the Constitution is known as the 'Mini Constitution' due to the extent of changes it introduced?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, made sweeping changes to the Constitution and is popularly known as the 'Mini Constitution'.

questions.sub: Panchayati Raj and urban local bodies (73rd and 74th Amendments)
questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions, inserted which new Part into the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) titled 'The Panchayats' and added the Eleventh Schedule.

questions.sub: Panchayati Raj and urban local bodies (73rd and 74th Amendments)
questions.question: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, deals with which subject?
questions.explanation: The 74th Amendment Act, 1992, gave constitutional status to Municipalities by inserting Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule.

questions.sub: Constitutional bodies: EC, CAG, UPSC, Finance Commission
questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is appointed by:
questions.explanation: Under Article 148, the CAG is appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal.

questions.sub: Constitutional bodies: EC, CAG, UPSC, Finance Commission
questions.question: The Finance Commission of India is constituted by the President under which Article, typically every five years?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission every five years to recommend distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States.

questions.sub: Article 371G and the special provisions for Mizoram
questions.question: Article 371G, which contains special provisions for the State of Mizoram, protects the application of which of the following without the concurrence of the State Legislative Assembly?

options.A: Mizo religious or social practices, Mizo customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice involving Mizo customary law, and ownership and transfer of land
options.B: Only the Mizo language as the medium of instruction
options.C: Only reservation of seats in the Assembly for Scheduled Tribes
options.D: Only the boundaries of Aizawl district

questions.explanation: Article 371G, inserted by the 53rd Amendment Act, 1986, along with the Mizoram Peace Accord, provides that Acts of Parliament shall not apply to Mizoram in respect of Mizo religious/social practices, customary law and procedure, administration of civil/criminal justice involving Mizo customary law, and ownership/transfer of land, unless the State Legislative Assembly by resolution so decides.

questions.sub: Article 371G and the special provisions for Mizoram
questions.question: Article 371G was inserted into the Constitution by which Constitutional Amendment Act, as part of the arrangement that created the State of Mizoram?
questions.explanation: The 53rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1986, inserted Article 371G, giving effect to special provisions for Mizoram as agreed in the Mizoram Peace Accord.

questions.sub: Sixth Schedule and Autonomous District Councils
questions.question: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the administration of tribal areas in which states?

options.C: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Manipur

questions.explanation: Article 244(2) and the Sixth Schedule provide for the administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram through Autonomous District Councils.

questions.sub: Sixth Schedule and Autonomous District Councils
questions.question: How many Autonomous District Councils, constituted under the Sixth Schedule, exist in Mizoram?
questions.explanation: Mizoram has three Autonomous District Councils under the Sixth Schedule: the Chakma Autonomous District Council, the Mara Autonomous District Council, and the Lai Autonomous District Council.

questions.sub: Right to Information Act
questions.question: The Right to Information Act, which mandates timely response to citizen requests for information, was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Right to Information Act, 2005, came into force on 12 October 2005, replacing the earlier Freedom of Information Act, 2002.

questions.sub: Right to Information Act
questions.question: Under the RTI Act, 2005, within how many days must a Public Information Officer normally furnish the requested information?
questions.explanation: Section 7 of the RTI Act, 2005, requires information to be provided within 30 days of the receipt of the request (48 hours where life or liberty is involved).
